title: A pangenome of tetraploid wheat reveals the genetic architecture underlying domestication and genomic diversity for breeding.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.18466336 file list (CC-BY-4.0): 12 genome FASTA files of about 3.1 GB each plus 12 gene-annotation GFF3 files of about 120 MB each. Figshare 32213433 holds code only (Pan-genome.zip, 5.2 MB). HEAD requests on the project database's variant files: SNP VCF (variant call file) 12.0 GB, InDel VCF 589 MB, SV (structural variant) VCF 874 MB, joint VCF 3.4 TB. A 2 MB ranged read of the SV VCF parsed cleanly and showed exactly 736 sample columns (e.g. PI470991, TRI11505, XM000835) with real genotype rows on chromosome 1A.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: That 373 accessions were phenotyped for 32 traits (7 plant architecture, 8 grain, 17 abiotic stress), that 260 accessions have spikelet-number data, and that the phenotypes sit in Supplementary Tables 19-20. The Europe PMC supplementaryFiles endpoint timed out (one attempt at 120 s), and the NCBI OA (open access) service returned 404, so no phenotype table, units or per-trait counts were seen.

a1_downloadable.note: Genotypes download openly (checked). The phenotype labels exist only in Supplementary Tables 19-20, which could not be retrieved: Europe PMC timed out and the NCBI OA service returned 404. Paper only.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Trait values are presumably one column per trait in Supplementary Table 19/20, so nothing would need constructing. Not verified because the table could not be opened.

a3_inputs_present.note: Genotypes are present as VCF files covering 736 samples (header checked in the SV file). No accession lookups needed.

a4_units_stated.note: Units for the 32 traits are unknown because the phenotype table was not retrievable. Abiotic-stress traits are often relative indices, so units can't be assumed.

a5_enough_rows.note: The paper says 373 phenotyped accessions (260 for spikelet number). The unit of prediction is the accession, so this is below the 400-row floor even for classification and far below 1,500 for regression. The 736 genotyped accessions don't help, because half have no labels.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: SV VCF 874 MB compressed; SNP VCF 12 GB would need thinning by streaming
a6_fits_laptop.note: Feasible if you use the SV or InDel VCF, or stream and LD-thin (drop correlated neighbouring variants from) the 12 GB SNP VCF down to roughly 50k markers × 373 lines.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: VCF sample count is 736, matching the 736 accessions in the abstract (checked). The 373 phenotyped count could not be checked.

a8_label_provenance.note: Labels are field or greenhouse measurements of plant traits, not model outputs (paper only).

existing_models.name: GBLUP (genomic best linear unbiased prediction) vs multi-trait deep learning on 270 durum wheat lines in 43 environments (Frontiers in Plant Science 2019, PMC6856087)
existing_models.score_and_split: GBLUP was best and deep learning was similar, under cross-validation across lines and environments (search snippet only; numbers not retrieved).

backbone.name: None suitable; DNA language models (e.g. Nucleotide Transformer) aren't designed for genome-wide genotype-to-trait prediction across 373 lines
backbone.licence: Assemblies are CC-BY-4.0; licence for the database VCFs is not stated

integration.partner_dataset: Companion tetraploid wheat pangenome (Nature Genetics s41588-026-02680-1) or the durum Global Durum Panel
integration.join_key: Germplasm accession IDs (PI, IG, TRI numbers)
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Do structural variants predict traits better than SNPs across independently genotyped tetraploid wheat panels?

controls.positive_control: Btr1-A loss-of-function alleles should predict non-brittle rachis (domesticated vs wild).
controls.negative_control: Shuffle the trait labels across accessions.
controls.external_validation: None verified; a different durum panel would need ID matching.

honest_claim_h3: Among 373 diverse tetraploid wheat accessions phenotyped by one group, genome-wide SVs explain some trait variance beyond SNPs. With n this small, that is a heritability statement rather than a deployable predictor.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use genome-wide DNA variants of tetraploid wheat lines to predict their plant, grain and stress-tolerance traits.
plain_idea.train_on: Per accession: genotypes at DNA variant sites (SNPs, small insertions/deletions, structural variants) from VCF files covering 736 accessions; only about 373 have trait labels (paper figure, not verified).
plain_idea.predict: 32 measured traits such as plant height, grain size and stress responses, from the authors' field and greenhouse phenotyping (Supplementary Tables 19-20, not retrieved).
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Durum breeders could test whether structural variants improve genomic selection, but at this sample size the answer would be noisy.

ml_idea: Genomic prediction (GBLUP or ridge regression vs. adding SVs) of 32 traits across 373 accessions, with leave-subspecies-out splits.

effort.compute_note: Estimated only: stream the 874 MB SV VCF into a 736 × variants matrix, then fit ridge or GBLUP on 373 rows; nothing timed.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Open Supplementary Table 19 and count accessions with non-missing values per trait; if most traits have under 400, it's dead.

verdict_reason: Fails A5: only about 373 phenotyped accessions (paper text), and the phenotype tables couldn't be retrieved, so units and counts are unverified (A1/A4). The genotype VCFs for 736 samples are open and parse, but genomic prediction in durum is already served by GBLUP.
